explanation: Zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to release hydrogen gas and form zinc chloride.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Grey zinc granules in colourless dilute hydrochloric acid.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A colourless zinc chloride solution; the granules shrink as they're consumed.
beaker_view.observation: Bubbles of hydrogen gas form steadily on the surface of the granules, and the solution stays colourless throughout as the zinc is slowly used up.
